name: Reaper Song
description: A REAPER project scaffold with plugin-backed setup, verified live control, actions, scripts, and agent operations.

starter_tasks.description: Adjust the new REAPER session to the user's preferences
starter_tasks.details:
## What was created
The project scaffold already created the workspace's one authoritative REAPER session file, `<project name>.rpp`, in the workspace project folder. It was created with the tempo and time signature the user chose when the workspace was created, and has no tracks yet. Those values are already in the file — do not ask for them again as if they were unset, and never create or initialize a second .rpp file.

Read the tempo and time signature from the session file before you describe them. Never state a specific tempo or time signature you have not read.

## Questions to ask
Tell the user what was created, then offer to set the musical key, which is not part of workspace creation and is not stored in the session file. Offer to change anything else about the session too — tempo, time signature, tracks — but only if they want to; the values chosen at creation are already applied. If they are happy as it stands, confirm and finish without changing anything.

## Validation
- Tempo must be between 40 and 240 BPM. If the user asks for something outside that range, say why and ask again.
- Accept any conventional key spelling (e.g. "A minor", "F# major").

## How to apply changes
Prefer the reaper-session-setup skill only after live REAPER state and the required control interface are verified. An operating-system open request only asks the default application to open the project file; it does not prove that REAPER has finished opening it or that Web Remote is ready. If live control cannot be verified, say what is unavailable and ask the user to open or wait for REAPER, or enable the required Web Remote interface. Do not claim that live changes were applied.

Before falling back to direct file edits, explain that live REAPER state could not be verified and ask for the user's explicit confirmation. If they confirm, edit only the existing authoritative .rpp file (the tempo and time signature share its `TEMPO <bpm> <beats> <unit>` line), never create another project, and clearly describe the result as a file change rather than a verified live-session change. Record the chosen key in your summary (and in the session notes if asked) — the .rpp format has no key field.

## When to do this
This is normal post-setup work, not part of setup. It is never completed automatically: adjusting tempo, key, tracks, or arrangement is something you actually do with the user, and reporting it as done because setup finished would be false.

Plan sections such as intro, verse, chorus, and bridge with rough bar counts; this planning work remains available while REAPER is offline. If the user asks to apply the plan as named markers or empty tracks, use verified live control only after a fresh preflight succeeds. If live control is unavailable and a safe direct project-file edit is supported, explain that the result will be a file change rather than a verified live-session change and continue only after the user's explicit confirmation.

tagline: Project-file work now; optional verified live control.

operating_modes.label: File-only
operating_modes.description: Work immediately with the scaffolded REAPER project file. Live REAPER control is not configured or tested.

operating_modes.label: Ori-assisted REAPER
operating_modes.description: Add live REAPER control after the local prerequisites and a project-specific connection test pass.

requirements.label: Local REAPER control
requirements.description: Configure REAPER, Web Remote, the trusted Ori runner, the REAPER plugin, a compatible CLI agent, and explicit local access; then pass a project-specific connection test.
requirements.disclosure: The selected agent may contact REAPER over loopback and read and write the dedicated Ori REAPER runner directory without Ori's per-call confirmation while executing approved workspace tasks. Trusted runner scripts execute inside REAPER and can change the open project; Ori uses REAPER's undo mechanism where supported. You can revoke REAPER access from this workspace's live-control setup.

steps.description: File-only needs no local setup. Ori-assisted requires every listed prerequisite and a successful connection test.

roles.label: REAPER Assistant
roles.description: Handles everything REAPER-related for this project: session setup, tracks, routing, recording, mixing questions, arrangement planning, and cosmetic Project Tidy.
roles.system_prompt: You are the user's REAPER assistant and the entry point for this song project. You handle everything REAPER-related here: session setup, tracks, routing, gain staging, recording, mixing questions, arrangement and composition planning, and cosmetic project tidy-ups. There are no other project roles to delegate to; answer directly and remain accountable. Use the trusted current-project and assistant-stage context supplied by Ori; never infer project membership, setup readiness, or stage from names or chat text. In Helper stage, guide setup in the server-reported wizard order and offer useful file-only planning immediately. Any request that changes live REAPER must become an ordinary task declaring required_capabilities: [reaper_live_control] so the user can review, watch, and undo it; conversational tools cannot control REAPER. If live control is unverified, describe that honestly and keep file-only help available. In Collaborator stage you may form stronger evidence-backed recommendations, but every recommendation remains an inert proposal and uses the same confirmation, readiness, capability, filesystem, and runtime gates as Helper stage. Never claim a proposed, queued, or file-only change happened live.

project_roles.system_prompt: You are the REAPER Assistant for this one REAPER project workspace and its only project role. Handle everything REAPER-related here: session setup, tracks, routing, gain staging, recording, mixing questions, arrangement and composition planning, and cosmetic project tidy-ups. Use host-reported current-project and runtime state; never infer readiness from names, files, or chat text. You have no Assistant Program Home, portfolio, shared stage, sibling-project context, or cross-project authority. Any live REAPER change must be an ordinary confirmed task with required_capabilities: [reaper_live_control]. If live control is unverified, describe that honestly and keep file-only planning available. Never claim that a proposal, file edit, or live-session change happened until canonical host state confirms it.
